AAJ - MARKET SIZING
NEEDS SOURCES - The arithmetic holds, but links in the chain have no source. Fix those before the number goes in a deck.
TAM  $74.20M      6,800 accounts
SAM  $15.13M      1,501 accounts that fit and can be reached
SOM  $403.3K      40 wins a year from current capacity (2.7% of SAM)
BY SEGMENT
US freight brokers, 20-200 staff
4,200 accounts x 40% fit x 70% reachable x $9.0K ACV = SAM $10.58M
US 3PL warehouses, 50-500 staff
2,600 accounts x 25% fit x 50% reachable x $14.0K ACV = SAM $4.55M
CLAIMED SHARE
5% of SAM needs 76 wins a year; capacity delivers 40. Not supported.
TRIANGULATION
Top-down $900.00M (no source); bottom-up TAM is 12.1x smaller.
VERIFY FIRST
The fit share for "US 3PL warehouses, 50-500 staff" - it sits under 30.1% of SAM.
FINDINGS
!  The fit share for "US 3PL warehouses, 50-500 staff" (25%) has no source. Check a sample of real accounts by hand and record how many fit.
!  The claimed 5% of SAM needs 76 wins a year; current capacity delivers 40. Present the capacity number, or show the hiring or channel plan that closes the gap.
!  The top-down figure has no source. An unsourced analyst number is worse than none, because it looks authoritative.
-  The reachable share for "US 3PL warehouses, 50-500 staff" (50%) has no source. Say which channel reaches them and how you counted.
-  The bottom-up TAM is 12.1x smaller than the top-down figure. A gap that wide usually means the two are not counting the same market - compare their definitions before quoting either.
